Definition: adverb from G227; truly:--indeed, surely, of a surety, truly, of a (in) truth, verily, very.
BiblicalUsage: Eighteen times, and it is the word for really and of a surety. Jesus sees Nathanael coming and says, Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile. And the Samaritans tell the woman at the well, Now we believe, not because of thy saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for truly carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the two confessions it carries, that Nathanael had no guile in him and the Samaritans knew for themselves who Jesus is.
